# Codex Plugin (codex-plugin-cc)

## Easy Read

**Analogy**: A plugin that has **OpenAI Codex (a different company's model)** audit the code generated by Claude as a "second opinion." Because an AI model grading its own output is highly susceptible to **sycophancy biases** (grading its own homework with an automatic A), this acts as a robust **cross-organizational peer review**.

| Term | Explanation |
|------|------|
| **Cross-Model** | Blending **two different AI models** together to bypass individual model biases |
| **Sycophancy** | The tendency of AI models to **blindly agree** with the user's or its own outputs |
| **Review** | Analyzing code to pinpoint **bugs, security vulnerabilities, or edge-case gaps** |

## One-Line Definition

An official OpenAI-developed plugin for Claude Code that enables **cross-model code reviews** by having OpenAI Codex audit the codebase modifications written by Claude.

## Core Philosophy

"An LLM auditing its own code triggers severe positive bias." To bypass this sycophancy trap, a competing model serves as the "second set of eyes." OpenAI releasing an official plugin for an Anthropic CLI terminal tool was a **historic industry first** that drew major attention in March 2026.

## Key Features

### Slash Commands

| Command | Functional Scope |
|--------|------|
| `/codex:review` | Executes a standard Codex code review on the active file |
| `/codex:adversarial-review` | Triggers a hostile security audit (injection vectors, auth gaps) |
| `/codex:rescue` | Delegates bug tracking and automated patch execution |
| `/codex:setup` | Configures environment variables and verifies authentication |
| `/codex:status` | Polls active background execution status |
| `/codex:result` | Outputs the result of a completed background task |
| `/codex:cancel` | Aborts a running Codex audit |

### Review Gate
An automated quality gate triggered via terminal execution hooks:

```
Claude Writes Code ──→ Codex Runs Review ──→ Bug Found? ──→ Claude Refactors
                                                                   │
                                                                   ▼
                                                            Codex Approves
```

When active, all terminal code modifications generated by Claude Code trigger a silent, background Codex review. If issues are flagged, the commit is blocked, forcing Claude to resolve the bugs first.

### Hostile Security Auditing
The `/codex:adversarial-review` goes beyond standard reviews to check:
- Hidden security vulnerabilities (e.g., OWASP top 10).
- Authentication and authorization logic flaws.
- Race conditions and parameter injection vectors.

## Installation

**Prerequisites**: Node.js 18.18+, ChatGPT subscription (Free tier supported) or OpenAI API key.

```bash
# Registering the plugin inside Claude Code
/codex:setup
# If the package is missing, it prompts a local npm install
# Authenticate via: !codex login
```

**Repository**: [openai/codex-plugin-cc](https://github.com/openai/codex-plugin-cc)

## Pros and Cons

| Advantages | Limitations |
|------|------|
| Cross-model reviews eliminate sycophancy and positive biases | Requires setting up a separate OpenAI account/API key |
| Built-in hostile security auditing is highly robust | External API roundtrips introduce execution latency and cost |
| Review Gate provides automated terminal-level quality control | Introduces tight coupling to two independent AI provider runtimes |
| Invokes a secondary model family without switching context windows | Purely reviews code (no generation or workspace planning features) |

## Significance in the AI-Native Era

The Codex Plugin implements the **Evaluator-Optimizer pattern** within [[concepts/ai-orchestration|AI Orchestration]]. Claude (the generator/optimizer) generates code, while Codex (the evaluator) scores it, feeding errors back to Claude for correction until the evaluation gate passes.

It highlights a major industry shift: AI tooling is evolving past monolithic systems toward **multi-provider, collaborative model networks**.
